title: POC Weekly Sync - Nova Logistics Pilot - Closeout
summary: Final POC weekly sync to review pilot results, confirm success criteria, discuss tuning that was applied (batching, KV cache, quantization), and align on commercial next steps. Redwood presented final metrics: 95% accuracy on intent classification evals, median latency 210ms for 256-token workloads on dedicated profile, and estimated cost reductions of ~38% with caching + quantization. Customer asked about on-prem roadmap, SOC2 artefacts, and rollout timeline. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send final report + optimized config, pricing for Dedicated, SOC2/ISO docs, and schedule exec review next week.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-02 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Priya Desai (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Nova/Head of ML), Carlos Rivera (Nova/Platform), Aisha Malik (Nova/Procurement), Tom Weller (Nova/Ops)

00:00 Priya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is our final weekly sync for the pilot, we're gonna run through what we measured, what tuning we did, and wrap on next steps.
00:12 Maya: cool thanks Priya. excited to see the numbers, we ran the last validation set this morning.
00:18 Liam: great, i'll start with the performance slide  so across the pilot we tested the customer intent pipeline with the 1.3B and 7B model families on the dedicated profile. median latency for realistic 256 token-ish requests landed at about 210 ms when we enabled prefix kv caching and continuous batching. without caching we were around 330 ms, so about a ~36% latency improvement.
00:42 Carlos: when you say continuous batching, is that the route-level batching we turned on? any impact on p95?
00:47 Liam: yes that's the route-level continuous batching - p95 moved from 620ms down to 410ms with batching plus the cache. there's still some tail on long sequences but overall better.
01:02 Maya: and accuracy? we need to be sure ranking/intent quality didn't regress with the quantized models.
01:10 Priya: quick summary there: we ran A/B evals on the final prompt set - intent accuracy was 93.8% on the float baseline, 93.2% on the 4-bit quantized 7B, for your business thresholds we hit the 92% bar so that's pass. we also included some hand-labeled edge cases from your returns flow, those held up reasonably.
01:34 Tom: that's good. on cost, what's the delta if we move to dedicated and keep caching?
01:40 Liam: estimated unit economics - with Dedicated and batching + prefix cache, tokens/second efficiency improves and we estimate ~38% lower cost per million tokens versus hosted default profile. i'll share the spreadsheet with the breakdown.
01:55 Aisha: procurement wants to see formal pricing and any commit options. also need lead times for dedicated capacity.
02:05 Priya: absolutely, we'll include an SKU based price table - short term reserved vs annual committed. lead time for Dedicated is typically 4-6 weeks once contracts are signed, less if we can allocate existing pools. we'll call that out.
02:20 Maya: on the private/on-prem ask - we did mention some regs around data residency. where's Redwood on on-prem or VPC private right now?
02:30 Liam: roadmap update: we have Redwood Private in GA for VPC-hosted control plane and an on-prem appliance option that's in preview. for Nova's needs, the VPC option provides network isolation + K-M-S integration for keys. the on-prem package needs a bit more security validation but it's possible; we can scope timeline post-contract.
02:52 Carlos: KMS integration - can you confirm which vendors? we use HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS in different environments.
02:59 Liam: we support AWS KMS today and have a Vault HSM pathway that we've done with a couple of customers - i'll capture the exact integration notes in the SOC/security pack.
03:10 Maya: any outstanding failures or edge cases from the pilot? we saw a handful of hallucinations in the long-response flows.
03:18 Liam: yes we logged those, about ~2% of long-form outputs, mostly around ambiguous returns descriptions. we tuned prompt templates and added guardrails (token limits, rerank) which reduced that to under 0.8% in the final pass. some of the transcribed notes mislabelled the model as rhyme-7b in earlier exports, that was a transcription hiccup.
03:43 Priya: that's helpful, thanks. i want to make sure the success criteria are clear for closing the pilot - from Redwood's side we had three: 1) hit >=92% intent accuracy on the evaluation flow, 2) median latency <=250ms on the dedicated profile for 256-token workloads, and 3) onboarding plan + commercial terms agreed. i'd like to confirm Nova's acceptance criteria.
04:08 Maya: that aligns; i'd refine the latency SLO to p50 <=250ms and p95 <=450ms, and also require a short reliability check - 99.5% uptime during working hours in the pilot window.
04:22 Tom: and ops wants a rollout playbook, so rollback steps, monitoring hooks (we use Datadog), and tracing keys.
04:31 Carlos: also need CI/CD integration notes - your model pinning and versioning approach.
04:36 Liam: absolutely - the platform supports model pinning and can do canary rollouts by percentage on the route. we'll include the rollout steps, Datadog tracing hook snippet, and a recommended alert set in the ops playbook.
04:53 Aisha: procurement - we'll need SOC2, ISO27001 evidence, plus typical legal terms. can you send those?
05:00 Priya: yes, we'll attach the security pack and standard contract redlines. we can also provide references for enterprise deployments.
05:08 Maya: on integration - we ran two scenarios: high concurrency (500 rps) and mixed batch (burst + steady). were there any stability issues at peak?
05:18 Liam: we saturated the dedicated pool at 520 rps in the stress test for ~10 minutes and saw queueing but no errors; latency spiked to ~900ms at the absolute peak. that's within expectation; we recommended an autoscale buffer or burst capacity to keep the tail lower.
05:38 Priya: did that model the on-prem env?
05:40 Liam: that was on Redwood Dedicated in our staging region; on-prem could differ depending on network and infra specs. we'd run a short benchmark in your infra during onboarding if you choose Private.
05:52 Maya: final question from my side - do we have a clear rollback path if quality drops after rollout?
05:58 Liam: yes - automatic fallback to a compatible model variant, and route-level config to pin to prior model version. canary monitoring can alert on quality regressions using your eval set.
06:10 Priya: great. last bit - commercial proposal cadence. i propose we send a final report and pricing today, schedule an exec review next week (30-45 min) with Maya + procurement + ops, and target a contract signature in 2-3 weeks if legal review goes smoothly.
06:26 Aisha: that timeline is aggressive but possible. procurement needs the full SOC2 and price sheet to start internal approvals.
06:33 Priya: understood - we'll send the pack today. Liam, any final technical caveats to call out?
06:38 Liam: just that the 4-bit quantization on 7B preserved quality in our evals but if you see any regression on unseen edge cases we'll pivot to mixed precision. also the KV prefix cache requires deterministic prompts to hit high cache rates - small prompt variability reduces cache hit rate.
06:58 Maya: good note on prompt determinism - we'll standardize the preamble.
07:03 Tom: action items for us will include running the internal security review and scheduling Datadog integration.
07:10 Priya: perfect. i'll summarize next steps and action items now.

Recap / Next Steps:
- Redwood to send final pilot report + detailed cost spreadsheet (today)
- Redwood to send SOC2/ISO docs and security pack (today)
- Redwood to provide Dedicated pricing SKUs and lead times (today)
- Schedule exec review (target: next Wednesday)
- Nova to run internal security review and Datadog integration test, confirm rollout window

Action items (brief):
- Priya Desai | Send final report + pricing + security pack | Due: 2026-06-02
- Liam O'Connor | Share benchmark / stress test logs and Datadog snippet | Due: 2026-06-03
- Maya Chen | Confirm acceptance of final eval set and SLO language | Due: 2026-06-04
- Aisha Malik | Start procurement approval with attached SOC2 + price sheet | Due: 2026-06-09
- Carlos Rivera | Schedule infra benchmark for Private if requested | Due: 2026-06-08

End of transcript.
